package.opener: What happens when a snake bites you? Venom from a venomous snake can cause paralysis that can stop breathing, bleeding problems, kidney failure and tissue damage (WHO). What to do while you wait for help (NHS): stay calm, keep the bitten part of your body as still as you can, take off rings and other jewellery in case it swells, and call your emergency number. Do NOT cut or suck the bite, do NOT tie anything tightly around it, and do not go near the snake. At the hospital, antivenom is the most effective treatment. Some bites from venomous snakes carry no venom at all, but you cannot tell, so get every snake bite checked. Worldwide, about 5.4 million people are bitten by snakes every year (WHO).

sources.note: 'An estimated 5.4 million people worldwide are bitten by snakes each year'; 'Bites by venomous snakes can cause paralysis that may prevent breathing, bleeding disorders that can lead to a fatal haemorrhage, irreversible kidney failure and tissue damage'; 'High-quality snake antivenoms are the most effective treatment to prevent or reverse most of the venomous effects of snake bites'.

sources.label: NHS. Snake bites
sources.note: Do: 'stay calm'; 'keep the part of your body that was bitten as still as you can'; 'take off any jewellery and loosen clothes near the bite, in case the skin swells'. Don't: 'do not try to suck or cut the venom (toxin) out of the bite'; 'do not tie anything tightly round the part of the body where the bite is'. 'you should get all snake bites checked as soon as possible'. Read in the browser on 2026-11-22.
